chunks: His words: 'Hadābiru's-sinin' (the thin camels of the years). This is the plural of 'hidbār', which is the camel made thin by long travel. So he likened the year to such a camel, in which drought had become widespread.
The Arab poet Dhū ar-Rummah said: 'These thin camels remain in their places, facing hardships, or we cast them into a barren land.'

key_terms.الْجَدْبُ: Drought, scarcity of rain and pasture.
key_terms.حَدَابِيرُ: Plural of hidbār, referring to thin camels, used metaphorically for years of drought.
key_terms.حِدْبَارٍ: A camel made thin by long travel or hardship.
key_terms.ذُو الرُّمَّةِ: Dhū ar-Rummah, a famous pre-Islamic Arab poet.

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Hadābiru's-sinin' in the context of the Sermon of Seeking Rain?
ai.summary: In this passage from the Sermon of Seeking Rain, Imam Ali employs the metaphor of 'Hadābiru's-sinin' (years of drought) by comparing them to thin camels exhausted by long journeys, a classical Arabic poetic image of weariness and scarcity. By citing the poet Dhū ar-Rummah, the Imam grounds his rhetorical appeal in the rich linguistic tradition of the Qur'an, highlighting the physical and spiritual desolation of the land. This imagery serves not only to describe environmental hardship but also to evoke the collective suffering of the community, thereby justifying the invocation of divine mercy.
